RECEPTIONIST
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Front Desk Manager (line)  ·  Coordinates with: Counsellor, Doctor, Housekeeping
Version 1.2

blocks.title: Page 2
blocks.text:
1  ·  Role Purpose
The Receptionist is the first and the last impression of the clinic. Every client is greeted, booked, 
attended and billed through the front desk, and the warmth, accuracy and discipline of that desk 
shape how the whole visit feels. The receptionist owns the front desk — greeting, appointments, 
calls, hospitality coordination, billing and records — to the standard the brand expects.
In one sentence.  Greet every client warmly, never lose an enquiry, keep the desk and the data clean, and 
make every payment transparent.
Reporting structure and key relationships
Relationship Type Cadence
Front Desk Manager (FDM) Reports to (line) Daily huddle + scorecard
Branch Manager Functional, above FDM Branch standard, monthly review
Counsellor Coordination Handoff, follow-ups
Doctor Coordination Check-in, scheduling
Housekeeping Coordination Hospitality, waiting-area readiness
Interim reporting note.  Until a Front Desk Manager is formally appointed at the branch, reception reports 
directly to the Branch Manager, who carries the FDM responsibilities. Once the FDM joins, the line shifts 
and the BM moves to functional oversight.
The desk sets the tone.  Reception is not a back-office function — it is the face of the branch. A client 
decides how they feel about the clinic in the first ten seconds at the desk and in the last ten seconds at 
billing. Hold both with the same care.

blocks.title: Page 3
blocks.text:
2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Six KRAs. Each carries weight in monthly review.
KRA 1 — Greeting & Client Experience
• Every client greeted within 10 seconds, by name, with a smile
• Warm, professional tone on every interaction
• Hospitality offered to every waiting client; client thanked on departure
• Positive feedback / CSAT above target
KRA 2 — Appointment Management
• Day's schedule reviewed before opening; dashboard kept open
• Bookings accurate — no clashes, no double-booking
• Confirmations sent a day ahead; appointments found by client name
• Coordination with counsellor / doctor / therapist on flow
KRA 3 — Call & Message Handling
• Calls answered promptly; ≥ 95% pick-up rate during duty hours
• Missed-call / callback log maintained; all missed calls returned same day
• WhatsApp messages replied to within the duty-hour SLA
• No enquiry lost — every lead logged and followed
KRA 4 — Billing Accuracy & Transparency
• Amount and purpose stated before every collection
• Bill / receipt generated and sent to the client's WhatsApp
• Billing accuracy at 100% — no errors, no disputes
• Zero off-system or cash-in-hand payments
KRA 5 — Records & CRM Hygiene
• Client contact and WhatsApp details accurate and updated
• Registration forms complete for every client
• Leads tagged correctly; every enquiry logged
• CRM data accuracy at 100%

blocks.title: Page 4
blocks.text:
KRA 6 — Front Desk Discipline & Brand Stewardship
• Grooming and uniform to standard; desk tidy; no personal phone at the desk
• Waiting area kept comfortable in coordination with housekeeping
• Zero hard-line violations — off-system payments, data mishandling
• Issues escalated to the FDM/BM rather than argued with the client

3  ·  Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Six core KPIs reviewed every day. Supporting KPIs reviewed at weekly and monthly cadence. Targets 
set within the first 30 days in role.
The six core Receptionist KPIs
KPI Target / Measure Reviewed by
Clients greeted within 10 seconds 100% (daily audit) FDM / BM
Call pick-up rate (duty hours) ≥ 95% FDM / BM

Why these six.  Reception's job is broad operationally — but these six are what a client feels every single 
visit. Hold these six daily, and the rest of the role falls into place. Lose the six, and the rest of the standards 
quietly drift.

blocks.title: Page 6
blocks.text:
4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure
Every working day follows this rhythm. The discipline is what makes the desk run.
Morning  ·  Before clients arrive
• Review the full day's schedule before clinic hours; keep the booking dashboard open.
• Ready the desk — forms, cards, stationery; switch on and check CRM, billing, phone, AC, 
lighting, music.
• Confirm with housekeeping that reception, washrooms and water station are ready.
• Join the reception huddle with the FDM (or BM, in the interim).
The 10-second rule & find-by-name
Greet in ten seconds; never ask for a phone number first.  A client should be greeted, by name, within ten 
seconds of walking in — warmth before paperwork. Appointments are always located by the client's name, 
never by asking 'give me your number,' which makes a client feel like a record rather than a guest.
Through the day
• Greet every client within 10 seconds, by name; locate the appointment by name and check 
them in.
• Offer water / tea / coffee; communicate any wait proactively.
• Answer every call promptly; maintain the missed-call / callback log; send WhatsApp 
confirmations.
• Bill transparently — state the amount and purpose, collect, send the WhatsApp receipt, 
record accurately.
• Keep CRM and records accurate; log every enquiry and tag leads correctly.
Evening  ·  After clients leave
• Confirm tomorrow's appointments and send confirmations.
• Complete all callbacks in the log.
• Reconcile and close billing with the FDM/BM; hand over cash securely.
• Update the CRM; tidy and lock the desk.

blocks.title: Page 8
blocks.text:
6  ·  Authority and Escalation
What Reception decides without escalation
• Routine bookings, rescheduling and confirmations
• Standard call and WhatsApp handling
• Hospitality and waiting-area coordination
• Standard billing within the published price list
What needs the FDM / BM
• Client complaint or a long-wait situation
• Scheduling clash that cannot be resolved cleanly
• Any billing query, discount or exception beyond standard
• System / dashboard issue
Clinical — to the Doctor (via the FDM/BM)
• Any clinical question from a client — never advise clinically
• Reaction or medical concern raised at the desk
Immediate escalation — hard-line situations
If you feel pressured to take an off-system payment or mishandle data — STOP.  Immediately. Step away 
from the desk before completing the transaction. Call the FDM or BM and brief them. Do not be talked out 
of it by the client. The 60 seconds you spend escalating is the 60 seconds that saves your job and the 
brand.

blocks.title: Page 9
blocks.text:
7  ·  Don'ts
Behaviours that are not acceptable, regardless of how busy the desk is.
• Never take an off-system or cash-in-hand payment
• Never lose, ignore or fail to log an enquiry
• Never share client data improperly
• Never argue with a client — acknowledge and escalate to the FDM/BM
• Never leave the desk unattended without cover
• Never use a personal phone at the desk in front of clients
• Never advise a client on a clinical matter
• Never treat a standard as optional because the floor is busy

Trigger Response

corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same 
KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-
ins
Three consecutive months miss Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR + 
FDM/BM
Lost / unlogged enquiries, repeatedly (3+ in a 
month)
Written warning
Billing error or dispute, repeatedly (2+ in a 
month)
Written warning; billing re-training
Single off-system payment Same-day investigation by FDM/BM + Saurabh; if confirmed 
deliberate, single-incident termination
Single data-mishandling incident (sharing 
client info, photos)
Same-day investigation by FDM/BM; if confirmed deliberate, 
single-incident termination
Pattern of grooming / discipline lapses Verbal warning → written warning → exit, per HR process
Serious dishonesty with the FDM/BM Single-incident termination consideration
On 'termination consideration'.  For off-system payment or data mishandling — the response is: same-
day investigation. If found deliberate, termination is the outcome. If found accidental (rare), formal written 
warning + re-training. The investigation is the protection — not a softening of the consequence.

blocks.text:
9  ·  First 30 Days — 10 / 10 / 10 Milestones
New receptionists deserve short-horizon markers. The following are what 'on track' looks like across 
the first 30 days.
Days 1–10 — Foundations Set
• Knows the 10-second rule cold and applies it on every visit
• CRM hygiene to standard — every enquiry logged, every call returned same day
• Billing accuracy at 95%+ — any errors caught and corrected before close
• Daily self-checklist filled without prompting
• Knows the day's appointment schedule cold before opening
• Zero hard-line violations
Days 11–20 — Independent Running
• Can run the front desk independently for at least a half-day
• Call pick-up rate at 95%+
• Billing accuracy at 100%
• Coordination with counsellor, doctor, housekeeping smooth — no friction
• Receives at least one positive client mention by name
• Confidence visible on the floor — calm even on a busy day
Days 21–30 — Holding the Standard
• Front-desk scorecard at 9/10 or above, sustained
• Zero lost enquiries; zero data mishandling sustained for 30 days
• Can train a newer receptionist on the 10-second rule and find-by-name
• FDM/BM confident leaving the desk in her hands for full days
• Self-checklist mastery — can move from daily checklist to weekly checklist if BM agrees
The 30-day signal.  If a receptionist is not at these markers by the end of day 30, that is a coaching signal, 
not a termination signal — but it cannot be ignored. FDM/BM decides on the next step with HR within 7 
days of the day-30 review.

blocks.title: Page 12
blocks.text:
10  ·  What 'Good' Looks Like — End of First Year
1. Clients greeted warmly within seconds, by name, every time.
2. No enquiry lost; callbacks cleared daily.
3. Billing accurate and transparent; receipts always sent.
4. CRM and records clean; forms complete.
5. The front desk feels calm, warm and in control even on a busy day.
6. Clients who come in asking for her by name.
The ultimate test.  When a regular client walks in and the receptionist's absence is immediately noticed — 
by clients, by counsellors, by doctors. That is what a good receptionist at GLEUHR looks like.
